title: Derivative-closed factorial seminorm versus quartic source-history growth
question: Can a factorial-weighted coefficient seminorm, which closes the source derivative at fixed radius, also control repeated insertion of the actual quartic Q3 source top monomial in both source orientations at a fixed positive final radius?
method: Rebuild the registered center and reverse source polynomials and extract the pure a^4 coefficient at q=v=0.
Define the finite-polynomial factorial seminorm sum_n |c_n| n! S^n and verify the exact one-step derivative closure identity.
Use the positive absolute-value top branch T=(51/140)a^4 D_a on the witness a and derive T^m(a)=(51/140)^m product_j(1+3j) a^(1+3m).
Evaluate exact rational norm ratios at S=1/4 and S'=1/8, compare the order-sixteen row with the 12-branch history baseline, and check a factorial lower-bound row.
Rebuild the polynomial and recurrence independently and compile Lean R290 for the rational fixtures and scope firewall.
finding: The factorial seminorm closes the formal source derivative exactly: ||D_a f||_(S,!)=S^(-1)||f||_(S,!). However the actual center and reverse source polynomials both contain the pure a^4 coefficient -51/140. The positive top branch T=(51/140)a^4D_a sends a to (51/140)^m product_j(1+3j) a^(1+3m). With S=1/4 and S'=1/8, the exact order-sixteen norm ratio is 16852401249880525043166743609120334459341208478260995138186151899470933533/244347413243905574267593745054566029721600, which exceeds 12^16=184884258895036416. The factorial lower bound grows superexponentially relative to every fixed exponential base, so this topology does not supply the required repeated-history envelope through the positive top-monomial majorant.
decision_reason: EXP-001117 rejected the pure radius-loss derivative architecture. This package tests the natural derivative-closed factorial replacement and shows that quartic source insertion, not the derivative alone, creates a separate superexponential branch. The route is therefore not admitted as a common-alpha/QFT topology without a proved full-Q3 cancellation or state-weighted suppression of that branch.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing route boundary. The result rejects only the positive top-monomial envelope in the factorial coefficient topology; it is not a no-go theorem for the signed complete Q3 representation, a different seminorm, common-core cancellations, QFT reconstruction, or any physical claim.

The -51/140 coefficient is rederived in both source orientations from the registered polynomial formulas.
The positive top branch is not identified with the signed full Q3 history; cancellations remain open.
The declared finite radius-loss row is exact, and the factorial lower bound supplies the asymptotic route boundary.
R290 checks only encoded rational fixtures and no unbounded or thermodynamic theorem.
